discussion_comments.comment_body: Agreed, fixed in 34056fc61. `HubStartupScreen` now renders the same title-bar shell as the onboarding overlay (`WindowTitleBarProvider` + `WindowTitleBar hostContent={false}`), so the window keeps its drag region, and frameless Windows keeps Minimize/Maximize/Close, before the app mounts and after a failure. The screen replaces the app rather than covering it, so only one set of controls is ever mounted.

Agreed, fixed in 58699c8a0. `App` stays mounted and is hidden with React `<Activity>` whenever the Hub isn't ready, instead of being unmounted. Hidden Activity content keeps its state, so the open conversation and selected session are still there after recovery. It also tears down effects and hides the DOM, including portaled dialogs and popovers, so they release their focus trap and body `pointer-events` while the startup screen shows (which keeps the fix for the earlier thread). Retry no longer brings `App` back early: it only reappears once `hub_status` is `ready`. `useHubStartup` also resets to `starting` when the transport drops, so a restarted sidecar's status is never read from the previous one.

Checked in the desktop app: with a conversation open and the provider dropdown showing, I froze the Hub and killed the sidecar. The startup screen replaced the app and Export diagnostics was clickable. After unfreezing, the app came back on the same conversation, and a new message streamed normally.

[P2] Preserve remote conversation selection when Activity resumes. Activity restarts effects when shown again, so App's get_process_context effect (lines 437–462) reruns after a transport reconnect. With an SSH environment selected, it dispatches select-environment-draft and navigates away from the open conversation to a blank draft. Reproduced with the existing effect and reducer: visible → hidden → visible changes the active thread from draft-1 (started session) to draft-2. Please make initial navigation bootstrap run only once after successful initialization, while allowing environment refresh on reconnect, and add coverage for an open remote conversation.

Good catch, fixed in 15d6388a0. The `get_process_context` effect moved into a small `useRemoteEnvironmentBootstrap` hook. A ref marks the first successful load, and refs survive Activity hiding. Every load (including after a reconnect) still refreshes `activeRemoteEnvironment`, but `select-environment-draft` is only dispatched on the first successful one. A load that fails or is cancelled before it lands does not count, so the next load still bootstraps.

Coverage is in `use-remote-environment-bootstrap.test.tsx`, using a real `<Activity>` and `desktopAppReducer`. It opens an SSH draft, starts it (`thread-started`), goes visible, hidden, visible, and asserts the active thread is still `draft-1` and `get_process_context` ran twice. With the ref removed it fails exactly like your repro (`draft-1` becomes `draft-2`). A second case covers a failed first load followed by a successful one.

That push also merges `main`. The merge had one real semantic conflict: #14653 added its own `get_hub_status` (the Hub settings panel), and this PR's startup-status `get_hub_status` would have shadowed it. Nothing in the webview used the PR's version (startup status comes from the replayed `hub_status` event), so I removed it.

Fixed in 7a9bf2ae36. ShortcutRecorder now calls suspendShortcuts() for the duration of a recording, and both QuitHoldHandler and the page-level shortcut listener check areShortcutsSuspended() before acting (the quit handler also cancels any hold in progress). The recorder also uses stopImmediatePropagation() so other capture-phase listeners on window don’t see the keydown. Covered by the “suspends shortcuts until every suspension is released” test in keybindings.test.ts.
Fixed in b4f6ae9e2. The dialog is now capped at the viewport height (`max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)]`) and scrolls, so Open Connectors stays reachable in short windows. Verified at 1280x420.

Fixed in 229051e. The restored height is clamped against window.innerHeight on load, and the panel has max-h-[80%] of the pane so a window shrink can never push the chat to zero; the ResizeObserver refits xterm when that cap kicks in.
